# Code Hosting and CI/CD: References

Always prefer each vendor's current documentation. Settings names, defaults, and plan availability
change often (especially for secret scanning and push protection). Re-verify links and contents when
updating this skill.

Last verified: 2026-10-31

## Vendor (authoritative)

- GitHub
  - Secure use reference for GitHub Actions (GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, SHA pinning, `pull_request_target`
    and `workflow_run`, script injection, self-hosted runners, OIDC, CODEOWNERS for workflows):
    https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use
  - Adding self-hosted runners (recommendation to use them only with private repositories):
    https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-runners/self-hosted-runners/add-runners
  - About push protection (user-level default for public repositories, repository-level enablement,
    bypass behavior): https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/about-push-protection
  - Managing personal access tokens (fine-grained vs. classic, expiry):
    https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens
  - Security advisories for GitHub Enterprise Server: see the GHES release notes for the installed
    version, https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server/admin/release-notes
- GitLab
  - GitLab Runner security (executors, privileged mode, pull policies, cloned runners, `GIT_STRATEGY`):
    https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/security/
  - Security releases: https://about.gitlab.com/releases/categories/releases/
  - Hardening recommendations for self-managed: https://docs.gitlab.com/security/hardening/
- Gitea
  - Configuration cheat sheet (`HTTP_PORT`, `START_SSH_SERVER`, `DISABLE_REGISTRATION`,
    `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW`, `INSTALL_LOCK`, `[actions]` `DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL`, `ENABLE_SWAGGER`,
    allowed-host lists): https://docs.gitea.com/administration/config-cheat-sheet
  - Security releases and advisories: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/security/advisories and
    https://blog.gitea.com/
- Forgejo
  - Securing Forgejo Actions deployments (runner labels `host`, `lxc`, `docker`; `container.privileged`,
    `container.network`, `valid_volumes`; forks and `pull_request_target`; ephemeral runners):
    https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/actions/security/
  - Runner installation (remote code execution warning, `DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL` name conflicts):
    https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/actions/runner-installation/
  - Releases and security announcements: https://forgejo.org/releases/
- Jenkins
  - Securing Jenkins (controller isolation, access control, CSRF, markup formatter, credentials):
    https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/security/
  - Script console (administrator-equivalent; decrypts credentials; may bypass audit):
    https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/managing/script-console/
  - Exposed services and ports (8080, agent listener and 50000 in Docker images, SSH server, removed
    UDP discovery): https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/security/services/
  - Security advisories: https://www.jenkins.io/security/advisories/
- Scanners (use their own docs for current flags and data handling)
  - Dependabot: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot
  - Renovate: https://docs.renovatebot.com/
  - Trivy: https://trivy.dev/
  - Grype: https://github.com/anchore/grype
  - Snyk CLI: https://docs.snyk.io/developer-tools/snyk-cli

Generic vulnerability and incident sources (CISA KEV, NVD, CVE, CISA ransomware guidance, IC3) are listed in
the core documents.

## Third-party (not authoritative)

- OpenSSF Scorecard (automated checks for branch protection, pinned dependencies, token permissions,
  dangerous workflows): https://github.com/ossf/scorecard
  Useful as a second opinion on public repositories; its checks are heuristics, and a high score is not
  proof of safety.
- gitleaks (local secret scanning): https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
  Read-only against a clone; output contains secrets, so handle it as secret material.
